newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC eyes gold market as treasury expands.
newsitem.headline: HSBC eyes gold market as treasury expands.

text.p: Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp (HSBC) plans to boost its presence in the Hong Kong gold market as part of its treasury expansion, the bank's treasury chief said on Friday.

"The focus we are starting to put on our bullion business is consistent with the continued upgrade of our capabilities in all treasury products," Michael Hillier, head of foreign exchange and institutional sales at HSBC Markets, told Reuters.
HSBC Markets, the treasury arm of HSBC, hired an experienced gold trader last month to boost HSBC's profile in the bullion market, Hillier said.
UK-based Midland Bank, a subsidiary of HSBC Holdings and well established in the bullion market, would support the department in their efforts, Hillier said.
"If we are successful in attracting new business, then we will probably be involved in the (bullion) market place a little bit more aggressively than we are now," Hillier said.
Hillier said China offered a great deal of potential for all treasury products, noting that HSBC expected to make inroads in China's bullion markets as well.
Gold traders in Hong Kong welcomed the move, noting that Midland would forge a link it lacked in the global gold trade.
"Anybody who is big in the business has to be here," said a senior gold source.
Several firms have withdrawn from Hong Kong's gold market over the past year, restructuring their operations in a moribund bullion environment.
